narr: Hurricane Francine made landfall along the Louisiana coast during the afternoon of September 11. Downgraded to a tropical depression as it moved northward through Mississippi the next day, Francine brought gradient wind gusts of 30-40 mph to Central Alabama. Numerous trees were downed across several counties, with some falling on power lines and across roadways. One minor injury occurred in Jefferson County when a tree fell onto a passing pickup truck.||The next couple days brought bands of heavy rainfall and gusty winds to the area as activity became increasing associated with a nearly stationary surface boundary. One storm in Blount County on the 13th produced hail over quarter-size, with another storm shortly after causing an area of tree and minor structural damage near Locust Fork. Heavy rainfall caused flooding issues in Birmingham the morning of the 14th, in Eufaula around midday on the 14th, and in Birmingham again just after midnight on the 15th.
ev: Heavy rainfall caused flooding in Birmingham, with a few roadways becoming temporarily impassable. Calls were received of vehicles stuck in floodwater along Green Springs Highway, Messer Airport Highway, and at the intersection of 31st St N and Rev Abraham Woods Jr Blvd.

Heavy rainfall flooded portions of Eufaula, including North Randolph Avenue, West Broad Street, Cherry Street, Colmont Drive, and South Eufaula Avenue. Areas near the intersection of North Orange Street and Britt Place and along Gammage Road were washed out by high water, creating large holes.

Multiple water rescues in vehicles occurred overnight in Birmingham following heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding. Several roadways in neighborhoods on the west side of downtown Birmingham were flooded, resulting in several calls concerning vehicles stranded in water. Interstate 59/20 was briefly flooded near Arkadelphia Rd. Village Creek and Valley Creek also quickly rose into Flood Stage between midnight and 2 am. A couple reports were received on the east side of downtown near the airport as well, notably along Appalachee St and Messer Airport Highway.
